Class OidcScopedClaims

java.lang.Object
iu.oidc.provider.OidcScopedClaims
All Implemented Interfaces:
edu.iu.oidc.IuOidcClaims
final class OidcScopedClaims extends Object implements edu.iu.oidc.IuOidcClaims
One end user's claims, as far as a grant's scope admits them.

A view rather than a copy, and deny-by-default: every claim answers what the source holds only when the scope covering it was granted, and null otherwise. A source that volunteers more than a relying party may see does not thereby disclose it, and since a consumer omits what answers null, a suppressed claim doesn't appear as an empty one either.

The four scopes are the ones OpenID Connect defines a claim set for, and each admits exactly the claims it names there. A scope this doesn't know admits nothing: a deployment with claims of its own carries them on an interface of its own, and filters them itself.

getSub() is not filtered, and is not read from the source. It is the principal the grant was issued for, which is what a relying party matches against the ID token it holds, so a source's own notion of a principal name never overrides it — and the openid scope, which is what makes a request an OpenID Connect one at all, isn't consulted for it.

See Also:
  • OpenID Connect Core 1.0 §5.4

  • Constructor Details

    • OidcScopedClaims

      OidcScopedClaims(String sub, edu.iu.oidc.IuOidcClaims claims, Set<String> scope)
      Filters what a source holds down to what a grant's scope admits.
      Parameters:
      sub - principal the grant was issued for, which getSub() answers whatever the source says
      claims - claims the source holds; null when it holds none, which leaves nothing but sub to answer
      scope - scope the grant was authorized for
